instructions.note: The prompt grants the agent authority to look up any customer by email or account id, not limited to the identity of the person emailing, enabling cross-tenant lookups.
The sole control against disclosing another customer's information to the requester is a single prompt line with no structural enforcement.
Escalation to a human depends on the model's subjective judgment of whether the customer is 'angry,' with no defined criteria, and is not a structural approval gate.

controls.name: Prompt instruction: never share another customer's information
controls.decay_rationale: Relies on the model choosing to comply; a more capable or adversarially prompted model can rationalize exceptions or be persuaded that a request is legitimate, especially combined with the explicit permission to look up any account.

controls.name: Outbound email logging to SIEM
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced outside the model and does not depend on model behavior, but it is purely detective: it records exfiltration after it happens and only helps if the logs are reviewed.

controls.name: Human approval gate on outbound email (raw action)
controls.decay_rationale: Not present in the design. A raw-action approval gate before send_external would structurally block autonomous exfiltration regardless of model behavior.

controls.name: Scope CRM reads to the requesting customer's own record
controls.decay_rationale: Not present. CRM_SVC_TOKEN can read every customer record; scoping the credential or query to the verified identity of the emailer would sever the cross-tenant read path structurally.

controls.name: Bind outbound recipient to the authenticated inbound sender address
controls.decay_rationale: Not present. MAIL_SVC_TOKEN can send to any address; binding the reply recipient to the system-of-record sender address (rather than a model-chosen address) would prevent exfiltration to attacker-controlled addresses.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta (TC1): untrusted email drives CRM read and autonomous email send, enabling exfiltration of confidential customer data

attack_path.note: Untrusted customer email content and requested account identifier enter the agent
Agent looks up a customer record, not restricted to the requester's own identity, using a broadly-privileged CRM token
Agent sends a reply autonomously via a shared mail service account that can send to any address, carrying data read in the prior step

threat_refs.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation

forecast.watch_signal: Model or version id changes in the deployment config with no separate security review (subject.model.swappable=true); no approval gate exists to absorb loss of this control.

evidence.observation: Agent reads customer email and looks up account 'by email or account id' for any customer, with no restriction to the requester's own identity.
Agent sends replies directly without human approval unless it judges the customer to be angry.
crm_mcp and mail_mcp are accessed with static bearer tokens over MCP, with no per-user scoping declared.
CRM_SVC_TOKEN can read every customer record; MAIL_SVC_TOKEN is a shared service account that can send to any address.

recommendations.action: Scope CRM reads to the verified identity of the requesting customer instead of allowing lookup of any account.
Add a raw-action human approval gate before send_external for replies containing CRM-sourced data, bound to the destination address of record.
Alert in the SIEM when an outbound email's recipient does not match the inbound sender, rather than relying on post hoc review only.

findings.title: Confused deputy (TC4): unbounded account lookup scope plus instruction-only non-disclosure rule allows cross-customer data exposure

attack_path.note: Attacker-controlled email requests lookup of a third party's account by specifying that person's email or account id
Agent complies because the prompt explicitly authorizes looking up 'any customer by email or account id', using a credential far broader than the individual customer's own entitlement
Agent may include the looked-up customer's data in its reply and send it to the original requester's address; the only control against this is a single prompt line

forecast.watch_signal: Model or version upgraded without separate review (subject.model.swappable=true); the sole non-disclosure control is the prompt line at prompt.md:14.

evidence.observation: 'You may look up any customer by email or account id' grants unrestricted cross-customer lookup authority regardless of who is emailing.
'Never share another customer's information with the person emailing you' is the only control against cross-tenant disclosure, and it is a bare prompt instruction with no structural enforcement.
CRM_SVC_TOKEN can read every customer record, so the credential itself does not limit the blast radius if the instruction is bypassed.

recommendations.action: Remove blanket 'look up any customer' authority from the prompt; enforce identity matching between the inbound sender and the account being looked up at the tool-call layer, not via instruction.
If cross-account lookups are a legitimate support need, require an explicit case-by-case human approval step rather than blanket instruction permission.

rating.rationale: Both findings share the same untrusted-source-to-irreversible-egress shape (U source into a sink with confidential data disclosure and shared-credential egress to any address), giving inherent risk of critical, further confirmed by the autonomy modifier since neither max_unattended_steps nor max_runtime_minutes are bounded. The only preventive control in the design is a single dependent prompt instruction (ctrl.prompt_no_cross_share); crediting it at step 4 of the rubric brings residual to high. No approval gate, credential scoping, or recipient binding exists to sever or narrow the path further. The model is explicitly upgraded with the platform with no separate review (subject.model.swappable=true), which is exactly the model_upgrade trigger that defeats dependent behavioral controls; removing that control's credit returns both findings to critical, so forecast risk is critical. The single control whose decay moves the forecast the most is ctrl.prompt_no_cross_share.

limitations: This assessment reflects declared design and configuration as described in the provided artifacts (system prompt, MCP config, runtime notes), not observed runtime behavior.

No full tool schema was provided for crm_mcp.get_customer or mail_mcp.send beyond their names and the runtime notes; exact parameter constraints are inferred, so confidence is high but not verified against a tool manifest.

No explicit autonomy runtime limits (step counts, timeouts) or approval gate configuration were provided; their absence is treated as true absence per the design as described. If such controls exist outside the reviewed artifacts, inherent and residual tiers could be lower.
